cards.back: A strong muscle that pumps blood around your body.
cards.say: heart. A strong muscle that pumps blood around your body.

cards.back: The heart, blood vessels and blood. It carries oxygen and nutrients around the body.
cards.say: circulatory system. The heart, blood vessels and blood. It carries oxygen and nutrients around the body.

cards.back: A tube that carries blood around the body.
cards.say: blood vessel. A tube that carries blood around the body.

cards.back: A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart.
cards.say: artery. A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart.

cards.back: A blood vessel that carries blood back to the heart.
cards.say: vein. A blood vessel that carries blood back to the heart.

cards.back: A tiny blood vessel. Oxygen and nutrients pass through its thin wall into the body's cells.
cards.say: capillary. A tiny blood vessel. Oxygen and nutrients pass through its thin wall into the body's cells.

cards.back: Two organs in your chest that take oxygen from the air into your blood.
cards.say: lungs. Two organs in your chest that take oxygen from the air into your blood.

cards.front: Which gas do we need from the air we breathe in?
cards.back: Oxygen. Your cells use it to release energy from food.
cards.say: Which gas do we need from the air we breathe in? Oxygen. Your cells use it to release energy from food.

cards.front: Which waste gas does your body breathe out?
cards.back: Carbon dioxide. It is made by the body's cells and carried to the lungs.
cards.say: Which waste gas does your body breathe out? Carbon dioxide. It is made by the body's cells and carried to the lungs.

cards.back: The windpipe. It carries air from your nose and mouth down to your lungs.
cards.say: trachea. The windpipe. It carries air from your nose and mouth down to your lungs.

cards.back: Two tubes that branch from the trachea, one going into each lung.
cards.say: bronchi. Two tubes that branch from the trachea, one going into each lung.

cards.back: Tiny air sacs in the lungs. Oxygen passes into the blood here and carbon dioxide passes out.
cards.say: alveoli. Tiny air sacs in the lungs. Oxygen passes into the blood here and carbon dioxide passes out.

cards.back: A sheet of muscle under the lungs. It moves down when you breathe in.
cards.say: diaphragm. A sheet of muscle under the lungs. It moves down when you breathe in.

cards.front: What happens in your chest when you breathe in?
cards.back: The ribs move up and out and the diaphragm moves down. The chest gets bigger, so air rushes in.
cards.say: What happens in your chest when you breathe in? The ribs move up and out and the diaphragm moves down. The chest gets bigger, so air rushes in.

cards.front: What happens in your chest when you breathe out?
cards.back: The ribs move down and in and the diaphragm moves up. The chest gets smaller, so air is pushed out.
cards.say: What happens in your chest when you breathe out? The ribs move down and in and the diaphragm moves up. The chest gets smaller, so air is pushed out.

cards.back: The beat you can feel where an artery is close to the skin. It is caused by the heart pumping.
cards.say: pulse. The beat you can feel where an artery is close to the skin. It is caused by the heart pumping.

cards.front: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
cards.back: Your muscles need more oxygen, so the heart pumps blood around faster.
cards.say: Why does your heart beat faster when you run? Your muscles need more oxygen, so the heart pumps blood around faster.

cards.front: Why do you breathe faster when you exercise?
cards.back: Your body needs more oxygen and has to get rid of more carbon dioxide.
cards.say: Why do you breathe faster when you exercise? Your body needs more oxygen and has to get rid of more carbon dioxide.

cards.back: Cells in the blood that carry oxygen around the body.
cards.say: red blood cells. Cells in the blood that carry oxygen around the body.

cards.front: What does blood carry besides oxygen?
cards.back: Nutrients from digested food, and waste carbon dioxide.
cards.say: What does blood carry besides oxygen? Nutrients from digested food, and waste carbon dioxide.

cards.front: Where does blood pick up oxygen?
cards.back: In the lungs, at the alveoli.
cards.say: Where does blood pick up oxygen? In the lungs, at the alveoli.

cards.front: Describe the journey of blood around the body.
cards.back: The heart pumps blood to the lungs to collect oxygen. It returns to the heart and is then pumped to the rest of the body.
cards.say: Describe the journey of blood around the body. The heart pumps blood to the lungs to collect oxygen. It returns to the heart and is then pumped to the rest of the body.

cards.front: Why is the heart muscle special?
cards.back: The heart muscle works all day and night without tiring, and exercise makes it stronger.
cards.say: Why is the heart muscle special? The heart muscle works all day and night without tiring, and exercise makes it stronger.
